newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate falls to 8.7 pct from 14.0.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate falls to 8.7 pct from 14.0.

text.p: The lack of term loans and the high volume of call money deals pushed down the Croatian average lending rate to 8.7 percent on Friday from 14.0 percent previously, dealers said.
Turnover rose to 41.2 million kuna from Thursday's 26.8 million, leaving a surplus of 74 million kuna on the supply side. Fresh deals accounted for 26 million kuna.
"Liquidity is still high but banks wanted to make sure there won't be any weekend surprises, so they sought call money loans to last through Saturday and Sunday," one dealer said.
Call money amounted to 29 million kuna, two-thirds of total transactions, granted at a low seven percent rate.
A small volume of fresh term loans were struck at 7.0 percent for one-week funds and 10 percent for two-week money.
Banks rolled over previous loans at between seven percent for one-week and 18 percent for three-month deals.
The central bank's kuna midrates for the weekend and Monday eased to 6.5472 against the dollar and firmed to 3.5699 against the German mark. -- Zagreb newsroom +385 1 455 7075
